body_long:
Louis Vuitton has unveiled its festive gastronomy collection for Christmas 2026, designed by Maxime Frédéric, named The World's Best Pastry Chef in 2025. Journal du Luxe reported the launch on 5 November.

## Spinning Blossom

The centrepiece is a set of round chocolates called Spinning Blossom, with a turning Monogram flower at their centre, a nod to the Monogram's 130th anniversary this year. They come singly or in boxes, in three colourways. Red pairs dark chocolate with a hazelnut praline heart and vanilla caramel. White combines dark and white chocolate, a praline with chocolate sablé flakes and a chocolate caramel. Green uses milk chocolate, a crisp matcha praline and a matching caramel.

## The mascot and the log

Vivienne, the house mascot, returns in a ski version in dark and white chocolate, with a crisp hazelnut gianduja, coated hazelnuts and a hazelnut praline. Fir-tree chocolates in several flavours complete the range.

The 2026 yule log layers biscuit, a confit, chestnut cream with Tahitian vanilla, orange and mandarin, and a milk jam infused with Earl Grey tea. Its silhouette carries the house's handwritten signature and a Monogram flower detail. No prices have been published.

## Where to find it

The collection is sold at Le Chocolat Maxime Frédéric at Louis Vuitton, 2 bis rue du Pont-Neuf, in the 1st arrondissement. Upstairs at the LV Dream exhibition space, the chef also runs the Café Maxime Frédéric at Louis Vuitton, launched in 2022.

Maxime Frédéric joined Plénitude at Cheval Blanc Paris, the LVMH hotel on the Seine, in 2019. According to The World's 50 Best, he works with both Louis Vuitton and Cheval Blanc, and also runs his own bakery, Pleincœur, in the 17th arrondissement.

## The signal

A palace pastry chef now designs a fashion house's Christmas. In Paris, the yule log has become a brand object, and hotels compete for the season's attention not only with one another but with the maisons. For palaces, the lesson is that a signature chef can carry a name well beyond the hotel's own doors.
